labels.label: lem:stability
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial, as the dispatch requires. MODEL: vol_g = √det G · μ, bvol_g = √det(PᵀGP) · μb_j and |∇u|²_g = du·G⁻¹du are the Riemannian formulas in a measurable frame (G the Gram matrix, P the boundary frame in the ambient frame, du in the coframe). The same μ, μb_j and P serve every metric, which is right because frames do not depend on the metric. F^(β) = (a_N·E + Σ_j β_j‖tr u‖²_{L^{p♯}(bvol_j)}) / ‖val u‖²_{L^{p*}(vol)} with a_N = 4(N−1)/(N−2), p* = 2N/(N−2), p♯ = 2(N−1)/(N−2): this is eq:trace-sobolev with c_N replaced by β_j (l.611). No structure field hides a conclusion: the fields are P_injective, val_one, tr_one, d_one and posDef. HYPOTHESIS: Comparable ε g g' := ∀ x, QFormComparable (1+ε) (G x) (G' x), which is exactly both quadratic-form inequalities at every point. The boundary comparison is derived through QFormComparable.congr, not assumed. CONCLUSION: stability proves (1+ε)^{−N} F_g(u) ≤ F_{g'}(u) ≤ (1+ε)^N F_g(u) for every u : D and every β ≥ 0 (N ≥ 3, ε ≥ 0). When F_g(u) > 0 this is the printed ratio; when F_g(u) = 0 it is strictly more. stability_ratio gives the printed ratio under F_g(u) ≠ 0, and finding 2 shows this hypothesis is forced. The pointwise lemmas: dual_le (B ≥ c⁻¹A ⇒ B⁻¹ ≤ cA⁻¹), det_le (through the spectrum of R⁻ᵀBR⁻¹), and sqrt_det_le/ge in dimensions N and N−1. The integrated exponents are the paper's: 1+N/2, (N−1)/p♯ = N/p* = (N−2)/2, and N in total. Each measure domination is used in both directions, so an infinite norm is infinite for both metrics, and the toReal-is-0 convention cannot create a spurious inequality. CONSEQUENTLY: adm_iff shows the competitor set does not depend on the metric under comparability. infF_le and le_infF give the two infimum bounds. tendsto_infF takes any filter along which the constants tend to 0. tendsto_infF_of_uniformlyClose reads 'g′ → g uniformly' as |g′(v,v) − g(v,v)| ≤ η·g(v,v) with η → 0. On compact Σ this is equivalent to C⁰ convergence, which is the convergence lem:gluing supplies at l.728. The reading is disclosed. WITNESS: toy_comparable and toy_stability compare G = 1 with G' = (1+ε)·1 on the two-point model. The model is genuine (vol = counting measure, mass 2; bvol = δ_false, mass 1; du = edge difference). FINDING 2 CHECKED, TRUE: 'all β_j ≥ 0' allows β = 0, and u = 1 ∈ W^{1,2}∖{0} gives F^(0)_g(1) = 0, so the printed ratio is 0/0 (toy_F_zero_one). On a connected Σ this happens exactly when every β_j = 0 and u is constant. It is harmless at l.728, which uses β = c_N and only the 'consequently'. Partial because the passage from a Riemannian manifold to the model waits on T-yamabe-scope. That instance should take D among finite-energy functions (minor finding 2).

labels.label: rem:sign
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial. CONSTANTS: cN = 2(N−1)·ω^{1/(N−1)} is eq:cN (l.338). ω = sphereArea N is the total mass of Mathlib's volume.toSphere, which equals N·|B^N| (sphereArea_eq); this is the area of the unit (N−1)-sphere. sphereArea_three gives 4π and cN_three gives 4√(4π). EQ:F1-TORUS: F_one is the first line with β, F^(β)(1) = Σ_j β_j Vol(B_j)^{(N−2)/(N−1)} / Vol(Σ)^{(N−2)/N}. Fq_one_round gives 2(N−1)·ω·Σ_j r_j^{N−2} / Vol^{(N−2)/N} assuming only Vol(B_j) = ω r_j^{N−1}, which is less than 'round, constant scalar curvature, minimal'. Fq_one_round_three gives 4·Σ_j 4πr_j / Vol^{1/3} (l.474). M is taken as its round-sphere value (l.467), as disclosed. FIRST VARIATION: hasDerivAt_normSq_one_add is l.734 exactly, 2ν(X)^{2/q−1}∫φ, for any finite measure, q > 0 and bounded φ. hasDerivAt_F_one_add gives the formula of l.739 for F^(β). In rem_sign it is specialised to c_N: 2c_N/Vol(Σ)^{(N−2)/N} · Σ_j Vol(B_j)^{−1/(N−1)} ∫_{B_j} φ bvol. Re-derived by hand: the gradient term is ε²E, and the denominator's derivative vanishes because ∫φ = 0. firstVariation_neg gives the strict sign from β_j > 0, tr φ ≤ 0 bvol_j-a.e. for every j, and tr φ ≠ 0 on a set of positive bvol_j-measure for some j. That is the paper's 'φ ≤ 0, φ ≢ 0 on ∂Σ'. CONSEQUENCES: exists_F_lt_F_one exhibits a competitor 1+εφ in Adm with F < F(1), not only a negative derivative. From it come infF_lt_F_one and infF_lt_Fq_one. kappa_lt_one proves ∀κ, κF(1) ≤ inf F → κ < 1, using F(1) > 0 when some bvol_j ≠ 0. rem_sign assembles (i)–(iv). ADDED HYPOTHESES, all disclosed: a cutoff χ ∈ D with tr χ = 1 on ∂Σ and ∫χ < Vol(Σ), used for (iii) and (iv). At the abstract layer it cannot be dropped: with D = ℝ·1 no admissible φ exists and inf F = F(1). It is the model form of the paper's 'Such φ exist' (l.741). Also bounded, measurable φ in place of smooth φ (a weakening), and finiteness/nonemptiness of vol and bvol, which are compactness and ∂Σ ≠ ∅. hround is always satisfiable (r_j := (Vol(B_j)/ω)^{1/(N−1)}), so it restricts nothing. WITNESS: toy_infF_lt_Fq_one with χ the indicator of the boundary point (∫χ = 1 < 2 = Vol). An auditor probe (stdin) checked F_g(1) > 0 on the toy, so the witness is not degenerate. The commentary sentence 'yields δ > 0 but no size' is not formalized, which is disclosed. FINDING 1 (eq:hoelder) CHECKED, TRUE. See build.details and minor finding 3. The REPORT files it under rem:sign because eq:hoelder is not a ledger row. When curating, the master session may attach it to lem:positivity, where the wrong constant is used (l.720).

build.details: `taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true` on Quotient.lean and on Stability.lean: exit 0, no output. The Quotient source was also re-elaborated through --stdin with three #print axioms appended, all [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. `lake build --no-build YamabeScaffold.Quotient YamabeScaffold.Stability` reports 'All targets up-to-date (8559 jobs)', so the oleans match the sources and nothing upstream moved. No lake build was started; pgrep found none running. grep for sorry, admit, axiom, unsafe, native_decide, implemented_by, extern, set_option and opaque: zero hits in both files, prose included. #print axioms probe on all 114 names in REPORT decls ∪ extra_decls, which are the 74 + 40 top-level declarations of the two files. It was fed through `lake env lean --stdin`, so no probe file was written, because the dispatch allows writing only this file. The probe imports Yamabe, YamabeScaffold (root), YamabeScaffold.Quotient and YamabeScaffold.Stability. Every name resolves with no name clash, and each depends on exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Imports: Quotient imports `Mathlib`; Stability imports `YamabeScaffold.Quotient`. The package is Mathlib-only (DEC-139). Every declaration is in namespace Yamabe, and none has 'Scaffold' in its name. A second stdin probe, an auditor check of finding 1, proves from hoelder_boundary_eq_one and normSq_one: for every measure ν with 0 < ν(X) < 1, ν(X)^{2/(N−1)}·‖1‖²_{L^{p♯}(ν)} < ‖1‖²_{L²(ν)}. So the printed l.609 fails at u = 1 for every mass in (0,1), not only for the point mass. The REPORT's note that the root YamabeScaffold.lean still imports only Basic is true. The axiom sweep sees these modules only after the master adds the imports, and graduation must rewrite Stability's `import YamabeScaffold.Quotient`.

docstring_contract: Both files have a title. Each cites its label unmarked with the ledger's line (`rem:sign` — `Yamabegap.tex:507`; `lem:stability` — `Yamabegap.tex:697`; both match ledger.json) within the first 4000 characters. ``**`label`**`` occurs nowhere. Each file has quoted > blocks, a Hypothesis checklist, a SCOPE (disclosed) section and the Provenance line. The SCOPE claims are true: abstract layer; finding 1 with its Lean names; normSq is 0 when infinite and x/0 = 0; inf over Adm; ω as the toSphere mass; M as the round value; the 0/0 case; the reading of 'uniformly'. The small defects are minor findings 1 and 2.

findings.what: Docstring contract (kb/0006). (1) Two quotes are cut short with no [...]. The eq:trace-sobolev quote stops at 'the trace of $u$' and drops ', which is well defined in $L^{\psharp}(\partial\Sigma)$ by the trace theorem.' (l.491). The rem:sign quote stops at '$\kappa<1$.' and drops the remark's last two sentences (l.509). SCOPE does say that the δ-sentence is not formalized. (2) The hypothesis checklist leaves out two Schwarzschild-like hypotheses that frame eq:F1-torus and rem:sign (l.467): constant scalar curvature, and ∂Σ minimal (H_g ≡ 0). The Lean does not use them (⚠ weakened). The REPORT records this; the module checklist does not.
findings.fix: Mark the cuts with [...]. Add a checklist row: '`g` of constant scalar curvature, `H_g ≡ 0` (l.467) | ⚠ weakened: not used'.

findings.what: SCOPE says that normSq is 0 when the norm is infinite, but not that `dirichlet` is 0 when the Dirichlet energy is infinite. Only its declaration docstring says so. Nothing proved here is wrong because of this: every theorem holds for the Lean F, the stability bounds are two-sided, and the toy model is finite. But the anchoring (T-yamabe-scope) must instantiate D with finite-energy, finite-norm functions (smooth functions on compact Σ, or W^{1,2}). An abstract D containing a function with infinite energy or boundary norm would give a Lean F, and so an infF, below the paper's.
findings.fix: Add one SCOPE line: '`dirichlet` is also 0 when infinite. The Riemannian instance must take D among finite-energy functions (C^∞(Σ), or W^{1,2} by density), where F and inf F are the paper's.'

findings.what: Finding 1 is TRUE (checked by hand and by a probe). The wording and the evidence can be tightened in two places. (a) The Lean counterexample is a one-point measure of mass 1/2, which is not the area measure of a sphere. The sentence that goes to the author, 'false whenever Vol(B_j) < 1', is prose resting on hoelder_boundary_eq_one. An auditor probe proves it in four lines (for every ν with 0 < ν(X) < 1, u = 1 violates the printed line). With u = 1 ∈ W^{1,2}(Σ), trace 1, this covers every round B_j of radius r_j < ω_{N−1}^{−1/(N−1)} (N = 3: r_j < 1/√(4π) ≈ 0.28). (b) 'Both uses at l.720 are qualitative (a norm tending to 0)' runs two citations together. Only the second (‖u_k‖_{L²(B_j)} ≤ Vol(B_j)^{1/(N−1)}‖u_k‖_{L^{p♯}(B_j)} → 0) uses the boundary line. The first ('bounded in W^{1,2}') and l.627 (lem:kobayashi) use the interior line, which is correct.
findings.fix: Optional.
